cards.text: Jotham has died, and his son Ahaz takes the throne of Judah. Ahaz is twenty years old, and he reigns in Jerusalem sixteen years. Chronicles holds him up next to one king from long ago: David, the one it calls his father.

cards.question: Like David his father, King Ahaz does what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, Ahaz walks in the ways of the kings of Israel. And he doesn't dip a toe in, friend, he CANNONBALLS.

cards.question: Ahaz goes all in on the ways of Israel's kings. What does he make?

answers.text: A bronze serpent on a pole

cards.text: Then it gets darker. Ahaz burns incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and sacrifices his sons in the fire, following the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

cards.question: Ahaz isn't keeping his worship to one spot. Where else does he sacrifice and burn incense?

answers.text: On the high places and under every green tree
Only inside the courts of the temple
At one altar on Mount Carmel

cards.text: So the LORD his God delivers Ahaz into the hand of the king of Aram. Aram attacks him and takes many captives.

cards.question: Where does the king of Aram carry off Judah's captives?
Aram isn't the only one. Ahaz is also delivered into the hand of the king of ___, who strikes him with great force.

cards.text: Israel hits hard. In one day Pekah son of Remaliah kills 120,000 valiant men in Judah, and Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, kills the king's son Maaseiah along with two of the king's top officials.

cards.question: Chronicles says Judah lost 120,000 valiant men in one day because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers.

cards.text: Then the Israelites take 200,000 captives from their own kinsmen in Judah: women, sons and daughters. They haul off a great deal of plunder too.

cards.question: The Israelites bring the captives and all that plunder home to ___.

cards.text: But a prophet of the LORD named Oded is there, and he walks out to meet the WHOLE army coming home to Samaria. Friend, back in the drawer I used to hide from a twist tie.

cards.question: Oded starts by telling the army why they won. Why did the LORD deliver Judah into their hand?

answers.text: Because of His wrath against Judah
Because Israel had stayed faithful to Him
Because Israel's army prayed before battle

cards.text: Then Oded turns it around: "But you have slaughtered them in a rage that reaches up to heaven." And now the army plans to make the men and women of Judah and Jerusalem their slaves.

cards.question: When Israel plans to enslave Judah's people, Oded tells the army that Israel has done nothing wrong before the LORD.
Oded tells the army to return the ___ they took from their kinsmen, because the fierce anger of the LORD is upon them.

cards.text: Back in Samaria, four leaders of the Ephraimites stand up against the soldiers coming home from the war. Among them are Azariah son of Jehohanan and Amasa son of Hadlai.

cards.question: The Ephraimite leaders tell the soldiers not to bring Judah's captives in. What's their reason?

answers.text: It would add to Israel's guilt before the LORD
Samaria has no room to house them all
Aram might come and take them back

cards.question: After Oded and the leaders both object, the armed men bring the captives into Samaria anyway.

cards.text: Instead, the soldiers leave the captives and the plunder with the leaders and the assembly. Then the men designated by name clothe the naked from the plunder, give them sandals, food and drink, anoint their wounds and put the feeble on donkeys.

cards.question: The men bring the captives back to their brothers in ___, the City of Palms.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Judah is getting nibbled from every side like the last cookie on the counter. The Edomites attack again and carry off captives, and the Philistines raid Judah's towns, capturing places like Beth-shemesh and Timnah.

cards.question: With enemies coming at him from every side, who does King Ahaz send to for help?
Chronicles says it was the LORD who humbled Judah through all these attacks. Why?

answers.text: Ahaz had been most unfaithful to the LORD
Judah's army had grown too proud
Judah had refused to pay Assyria

cards.text: Ahaz's call goes out, and Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, comes to him.

cards.question: Tiglath-pileser afflicts Ahaz instead of strengthening him.

cards.text: And Ahaz PAID for this help, taking a portion from the house of the LORD, the royal palace and the princes for the king of Assyria, and it did not help him. That's hiring a bodyguard and the bodyguard turns out to be your biggest problem.

cards.question: Ahaz is in distress and nothing has helped. In that time, he becomes even more ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: Then Ahaz sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him. Hold on. The ones who BEAT him?

cards.question: Why does Ahaz decide to sacrifice to the gods of Damascus?

answers.text: He thinks they helped Aram and might help him
He wants to make peace with Aram's king
Assyria's king orders him to do it

cards.text: But these gods were the downfall of Ahaz and of all Israel. And Ahaz keeps going: he gathers the articles of the house of God and cuts them into pieces.

cards.question: With the articles of God's house cut to pieces, Ahaz ___ the doors of the house of the LORD.
With the temple doors shut, where does Ahaz set up altars of his own?

answers.text: On every street corner in Jerusalem
Only in his own palace courtyard
Just outside the city of Samaria

cards.text: In every city of Judah he builds high places to offer incense to other gods. And so he provokes the LORD, the God of his fathers.

cards.question: When Ahaz dies and is buried in Jerusalem, he is placed in the tombs of the kings of Israel.

cards.text: The rest of what Ahaz did, from beginning to end, is written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. And his son Hezekiah reigns in his place.

findings.problem: The card says Jotham has died and Ahaz is his son. That fact is not in 2 Chronicles 28. It comes from 2 Chronicles 27:9, but the card cites only 2 Chronicles 28:1 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Ahaz isn't keeping his worship to one spot' rules out both wrong answers, 'Only inside the courts of the temple' and 'At one altar on Mount Carmel'. That gives the answer away. The right answer is also clearly longer than the other two.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Pekah appears here for the first time but is called only 'Pekah son of Remaliah'. The card never says who he is, such as Pekah, king of Israel, with its reference (2 Kings 15:27).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'He walks out to meet the WHOLE army' stretches the retelling. The text says only that Oded 'went out to meet the army that returned to Samaria' (2 Chr 28:9). The twist-tie joke then rests on Oded facing the army alone, which the text never says.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card marks as False that the armed men bring the captives into Samaria. But 2 Chr 28:8 says they brought the plunder to Samaria, and 28:9 says the army 'returned to Samaria'. The text leaves open whether the captives were already in Samaria, so a baker could argue that 'True' is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wording 'even more ___ to the LORD' rules out both wrong answers. Ahaz was never faithful, so 'even more faithful' cannot be right, and 'even more humble to the LORD' does not read naturally. Only 'unfaithful' fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 20 tells 2 Chr 28:26 after card 19 has already asked about Ahaz's burial in 28:27. This steps backward in the passage instead of moving forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
